what_worked: Crowded-vs-lucrative thesis is genuinely useful; Sales caveat and signal-quality slide show analytical maturity.
fix_next: Disclose how median 12-mo revenue was computed, acknowledge 27% missing categories, and reconcile figures with raw medians.
verdict: Strong narrative arc with a real thesis, undermined by unverifiable and likely inflated median figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: AI median 12-mo rev $4,301 doesn't match reference median $503 annualized ($6,036) or raw; Marketing $10,029 vs ref $2,369.50×12=$28,434; Education $14,300 vs ref $2,435×12=$29,220. Slide 2: Productivity listed at 49 companies with median $350 — 'Productivity' is not in the reference category set, possibly conflated. Slide 3: Content Creation called 'highest rev/customer of the four' but Sales ($102.9) is higher than Content Creation ($20.7) — contradicts their own Slide 4.

evidence.insight: Slide 2's crowded≠lucrative framing is original and decision-useful. Slide 4 adds per-customer value with honest n=13 caveat. Slide 6 trust-vs-skeptical signal framework goes beyond chart narration. Depth is good but not exceptional.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: AI overcrowding problem → alternative categories → operational playbook → signal quality → actionable summary. Each slide builds purposefully. Thesis lands cleanly on Slide 7. Synthesis is present.
evidence.framing: Audience (newcomer picking a category) is clear from Slide 1. However, 274 missing category values (27.4%) never disclosed. 216 zero-revenue companies not discussed. No survivorship bias mention. Scope is stated but limitations are thin, dropping from 6.5 to 6.
evidence.accuracy: Core median revenue figures cannot be reconciled with reference data under any consistent transformation (raw monthly, ×12, or otherwise). AI $4,301 vs ref $503; Marketing $10,029 vs ref $2,369.50; Education $14,300 vs ref $2,435. Category counts match reference. Slide 3 calls Content Creation 'highest rev/customer of the four' but Slide 4 shows Sales at $102.9 vs Content Creation $20.7 — internal contradiction. 'Productivity' and 'Sales' categories not in reference set.
evidence.visual: Consistent teal palette, clean card layouts (Slide 3), well-structured table (Slide 5), effective trust/skeptical split (Slide 6). Slide 2 line connecting categorical bars is misleading chart choice. Annotations are helpful throughout. No decorative filler.

change_reason: Lowered framing from 6.5 to 6: missing-data and zero-revenue omissions are more significant given 27% category missingness directly affects the category-focused thesis. Accuracy stays at 5: median figures remain irreconcilable and an internal contradiction exists between Slides 3 and 4. All other scores confirmed.
